title: The Parallelization Ceiling
equation: Max Speedup = 1 ÷ (Serial Fraction + Parallel Fraction ÷ N)
hook: Doubling the team almost never doubles the speed.
statement: How fast you can go is capped by the part of the work that has to happen one step at a time.
explainer: No matter how many people you throw at it, the steps that must happen in order set a hard ceiling. Past a point, more hands buy you almost nothing.
sop: Split your process into steps that can run at once and steps that can't.
Estimate the Serial Fraction of total time.
Calculate Max Speedup before hiring or buying capacity.
Shrink the serial steps by cutting, automating, or redesigning them.
Add people only until the ceiling makes more pointless.
equation_example: Serial Fraction 0.2, Parallel Fraction 0.8, 4 workers. 1 ÷ (0.2 + 0.8 ÷ 4) = 1 ÷ 0.4 = 2.5 times faster. Even infinite workers cap out at 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5 times. Shrink the serial part to raise the ceiling.
question: Write down the one step in your process that everything else waits on.
closing_statement: Fix the bottleneck instead of piling on more effort.
caption:
Principle Nº 356: The Parallelization Ceiling

Doubling the team almost never doubles the speed.

How fast you can go is capped by the part of the work that has to happen one step at a time.

Your turn: Write down the one step in your process that everything else waits on.
